narrativeReportMd:
# InsurancePlan R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes were found. R6 keeps `InsurancePlan`, but it is no longer the same combined product/plan container as R4: the product side moved to the new `InsuranceProduct` resource, and the old repeatable `plan` backbone was hoisted into one plan per R6 resource.

## Scope
The analysis compares the local R4 and R6 `InsurancePlan` StructureDefinitions and uses R6 `InsuranceProduct` only to confirm where removed R4 content moved. Inherited base-resource and datatype changes are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
The migration is a split, not a flat rename. R4 product fields such as `status`, `name`, `ownedBy`, `contact`, `endpoint`, and `coverage` should become `InsuranceProduct` data. Each R4 `plan` repetition should generally become a separate R6 `InsurancePlan` that references the product. Path-preserving transforms are especially dangerous for `identifier` and `type`, whose meanings changed.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact issues are the product/plan split, the removal of the modifier `status` from `InsurancePlan`, the removal of product metadata and coverage benefits from `InsurancePlan`, and the removal/hoisting of repeatable `InsurancePlan.plan`.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed for product matching, multi-plan splitting, identifier semantics, and down-conversion policy when R6 plans reference products or lack local identifiers.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The redesign is probably justified by normalization, but compatibility would have been easier if R6 had retained deprecated aliases or provided official conversion rules and cross-version extensions.

## Follow-up analysis
The `InsuranceProduct` resource, `ExtendedContactDetail` datatype, relevant SearchParameters, and terminology expansions should be reviewed separately for complete migration planning.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 `InsurancePlan` has substantial local breaking changes: R4 product-level fields moved to `InsuranceProduct`, repeatable `plan` entries became separate root-level plan resources, and `identifier`/`type` are not safe to map by path alone. The largest uncertainty is the absence of official conversion maps and terminology expansions.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should split each R4 `InsurancePlan` into product and plan resources, preserve modifier `status` on `InsuranceProduct`, explode multiple R4 `plan` entries into multiple R6 `InsurancePlan` resources, and apply source-path-aware rules for identifiers and type. Down-conversion from R6 requires dereferencing `InsurancePlan.product` or accepting loss/extension-based representation.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural element, cardinality, flag, and local constraint changes because both primary StructureDefinitions are present and the R6 `InsuranceProduct` counterpart is available locally. Confidence is lower for exact terminology code deltas and rationale because official diffs, narrative pages, and live terminology expansions were not provided.

findings.title: InsurancePlan was split from a combined product/plan resource into a plan resource backed by InsuranceProduct

oldState.summary: R4 InsurancePlan combined health insurance product metadata, coverage/benefit definitions, and repeatable plan details in one resource.

semanticText.definition: Details of a Health Insurance product/plan provided by an organization.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4 the assigned resource represented both the product and its plan offerings. Product-level elements such as `status`, `name`, `ownedBy`, `contact`, `endpoint`, and `coverage` lived directly under `InsurancePlan`, while repeatable plan offerings lived under `InsurancePlan.plan`.

newState.summary: R6 InsurancePlan is a narrower plan resource; product-level content is represented by the new InsuranceProduct resource and referenced by InsurancePlan.product.

semanticText.definition: InsurancePlan describes the costs to the subscriber or beneficiary associated with benefits... The specific benefits covered by the plan are described in the `InsuranceProduct` referenced in `InsurancePlan.product`.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the same canonical URL and resource type for `InsurancePlan`, but its meaning is no longer the same envelope as R4. Product metadata and coverage definitions are modeled in `InsuranceProduct`; R6 `InsurancePlan` carries plan identifiers/classification, product reference, coverage area/network, and cost details.

facts.note: The canonical identity is stable even though the business meaning and content model changed materially.

facts.newValue: Moved to R6 InsuranceProduct and referenced from R6 InsurancePlan

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 package retains `StructureDefinition-InsurancePlan.json` with the same canonical URL, and also adds `StructureDefinition-InsuranceProduct.json`. The R6 InsurancePlan root definition explicitly points to `InsuranceProduct` for benefits covered by the plan.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The identity-level change is not a rename or removal of the resource, but it invalidates a simple same-resource copy strategy. Many R4 instances use product-level elements or repeated `plan` components that are no longer legal at the same paths in R6. Conversely, R6 instances can rely on a separate `InsuranceProduct` resource and a `product` reference that R4 has no native slot for.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Insurance product status, payer ownership, network/coverage definitions, and plan costs are business-critical for eligibility and directory use cases. Misclassifying product identifiers as plan identifiers, or dropping the linked product, can change what coverage a member or subscriber appears to have.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate reusable insurance product/benefit definitions from plan-specific identifiers, areas, networks, and costs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 combined product/plan shape as deprecated content while adding InsuranceProduct and product references.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: product benefits and administrative metadata can be reused across multiple plan offerings instead of being repeated in every plan. A less-breaking transition could have kept the combined R4 `InsurancePlan` shape legal, but that would materially weaken the normalized product/plan boundary and require long-lived rules for when inline product data, nested plans, and referenced `InsuranceProduct` data conflict.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have added `InsuranceProduct` and `InsurancePlan.product` while retaining the old inline product fields and `InsurancePlan.plan` backbone as deprecated transitional elements. That would preserve many R4 instances, but it is only a partial alternative because it creates parallel same-domain representations and risks the deprecated combined shape never disappearing.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances but leaves duplicate product and plan representations with unclear precedence.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example illustrates the new resource boundary; real transforms need rules for splitting one R4 resource into one product plus zero or more plan resources.

findings.narrativeMd: The biggest InsurancePlan change is a local domain split. R4 `InsurancePlan` was a single container for product metadata, coverage benefits, and one or more plan offerings. R6 `InsurancePlan` is the plan-side resource and points to a separate `InsuranceProduct`. Existing code that assumes the same resource identity has the same content model will either reject old elements, silently drop product content, or attach product identifiers and types to the wrong business object.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A plain R4-to-R6 parse can fail whenever an instance includes now-removed product fields or a `plan` backbone. R6-to-R4 conversion is not a local field rename: it may require dereferencing `InsurancePlan.product`, merging data from an `InsuranceProduct`, and deciding how to preserve resource IDs, references, and lifecycle status.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Treat migration as a split/normalize operation. Create or match an `InsuranceProduct` for product-level metadata and coverage benefits; create one R6 `InsurancePlan` per plan offering; set `InsurancePlan.product` to the product; move R4 `plan.*` data to the R6 plan root; and test multi-plan R4 resources, missing product identifiers, and references from other resources.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The normalized model is probably justified by the need to distinguish products from plan offerings, but the compatible alternative would have been a transitional period where inline product fields remained legal and were marked deprecated. That would have preserved old instances but weakened the clarity of the new model.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding intentionally summarizes the resource-level redesign. The following findings call out the specific element-level mechanisms that cause validation or conversion breaks.

findings.title: Modifier element InsurancePlan.status was removed from InsurancePlan and moved to InsuranceProduct.status

oldState.summary: R4 InsurancePlan.status was an optional modifier code bound required to publication-status.

semanticText.definition: The current state of the health insurance product.

oldState.narrativeMd: `InsurancePlan.status` carried lifecycle status directly on the R4 resource and was marked as a modifier, so consumers were expected to account for inactive or retired plans/products.

newState.summary: R6 InsurancePlan has no status element; equivalent product lifecycle status is on InsuranceProduct.status.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 plan instances cannot carry `status` directly. The comparable status is located on the referenced `InsuranceProduct`, not on `InsurancePlan`.

facts.note: The modifier element is removed from this resource.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 InsurancePlan differential has no `InsurancePlan.status`; the R6 InsuranceProduct differential contains `InsuranceProduct.status` with the same lifecycle semantics and modifier flag.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance with `InsurancePlan.status` is no longer valid as an R6 `InsurancePlan`. The runtime risk is high because the removed element was a modifier: dropping `retired`, `draft`, or `unknown` status can cause user interfaces, caches, or eligibility logic to treat inactive products as active.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Using a retired or draft insurance product as active can have direct business consequences for plan selection, directory publication, and eligibility workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Attach lifecycle status to the reusable insurance product rather than each plan-cost variant.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `InsurancePlan.status` as a deprecated alias while also placing product lifecycle status on `InsuranceProduct.status`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving product lifecycle status to `InsuranceProduct.status` follows the product/plan split and is domain-coherent. The break is still significant because the R4 element was a modifier, but retaining it as a base R6 alias would require explicit agreement or precedence rules between plan-local and product-level status and could create safety-relevant ambiguity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could have kept `InsurancePlan.status` with deprecation guidance, possibly requiring it to agree with the referenced product status when both are present. That would let old R4 instances validate, but only partially solves the problem because duplicate modifier elements can conflict and consumers would need to inspect both locations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Compatibility aliasing would preserve old data but creates duplicate modifier status and conflict-handling risk.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `InsurancePlan.status` as 0..1 code, modifier true, summary true, required publication-status binding.
No `InsurancePlan.status` element appears in the R6 InsurancePlan differential.
R6 InsuranceProduct defines the corresponding product status as 0..1 code, modifier true, summary true.
evidence.quote: The current state of the health insurance product.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 fragment satisfies the local R4 identifier/name invariant but has a `status` property that is not legal on R6 `InsurancePlan`; status should move to the product resource.

findings.narrativeMd: `InsurancePlan.status` is a hard and semantically important removal. Because it was a modifier in R4, migration must not simply discard it. R6 expects the lifecycle state to travel with the referenced `InsuranceProduct`, so validators and generated R6 model classes will reject the old path while business logic must learn to consult the linked product.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances containing `status` become R6-invalid at the same resource path. R6 instances can preserve lifecycle status only if the `InsuranceProduct` is available; a standalone R6 `InsurancePlan` without its product is not enough to reconstruct the R4 status field.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move `InsurancePlan.status` to `InsuranceProduct.status` during the split. Audit consumers that filtered or hid retired/draft plans, because they must now follow `InsurancePlan.product` and evaluate the product status. Include tests for each publication-status code, especially `retired` and `unknown`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change follows the product split, but because modifier elements have special safety semantics, a compatibility alias or explicit conversion guidance would have reduced risk. The tradeoff is duplication if a plan-specific status ever needs to diverge from product status.

findings.title: Product metadata, contacts, endpoints, ownership, and coverage benefits were removed from InsurancePlan

affectedLocation.oldPath: InsurancePlan.name / alias / period / ownedBy / administeredBy / contact / endpoint / coverage

oldState.summary: R4 InsurancePlan directly carried product metadata, administrative references, contact details, endpoints, and coverage/benefit definitions.
oldState.narrativeMd: The removed R4 product-level subtree includes `name`, `alias`, `period`, `ownedBy`, `administeredBy`, `contact` and its child fields, `endpoint`, and `coverage` with coverage type, network, benefits, requirements, and limits.

newState.summary: Those product-level elements are not present on R6 InsurancePlan; comparable content is on R6 InsuranceProduct.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `InsurancePlan` no longer accepts the former inline product metadata. Product contacts use `InsuranceProduct.contact` of type `ExtendedContactDetail`, and coverage/benefit details are under `InsuranceProduct.coverage`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The removed R4 element names and definitions correspond closely to R6 `InsuranceProduct` differential elements. The R6 InsurancePlan differential omits these elements entirely.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance that uses the common product fields will fail R6 validation if sent as an `InsurancePlan`. Runtime/codegen risk is high because generated R6 classes no longer have these properties on `InsurancePlan`; conversion must instantiate and link another resource.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Ownership, administration, contact, endpoint, and coverage-benefit data are core directory and payer data. Losing them can misroute consumers or misstate available benefits.

justification.inferredGoal: Normalize insurance product metadata and benefit definitions into InsuranceProduct.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain old inline product metadata, contact, endpoint, ownership, and coverage fields on `InsurancePlan` as deprecated aliases.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 placement is coherent because these elements describe the reusable insurance product rather than a plan-cost variant. Preserving them on `InsurancePlan` would be less disruptive, but the cost is material: product name, contacts, ownership, endpoints, and benefits could be present both inline and on `InsuranceProduct`, requiring reconciliation and making validation semantics less clear.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A compatible base design could have allowed the removed R4 product fields to remain on `InsurancePlan` during a transition while encouraging use of `InsuranceProduct`. This would preserve many R4-valid instances, but it is only a partial alternative because duplicated product data can diverge and would burden servers and clients with precedence rules.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Reduces validation breaks but keeps two sources of truth for product facts.

evidence.detail: R4 defines product name directly on InsurancePlan.
evidence.quote: Official name of the health insurance product as designated by the owner.

evidence.detail: R4 defines coverage details directly on InsurancePlan.
evidence.quote: Details about the coverage offered by the insurance product.

evidence.detail: R6 InsurancePlan differential does not include name, alias, period, ownedBy, administeredBy, contact, endpoint, or coverage.
R6 InsuranceProduct contains the corresponding product coverage details.
R6 InsuranceProduct contact is typed as ExtendedContactDetail, not the old local BackboneElement.

examples.examplesMd: The example shows a structurally valid R4 resource fragment that must become an `InsuranceProduct` fragment in R6. Contact transformation may need datatype-specific review.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 product metadata and benefit definitions were removed from `InsurancePlan` rather than kept as aliases. This is a hard parser and validator break for old instances that included product names, payer organizations, contact points, endpoints, or benefit coverage details. It is also a codegen break because R6 `InsurancePlan` model classes no longer expose these properties.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances with any of the removed product fields are R6-invalid on `InsurancePlan`. R6-to-R4 conversion cannot be performed from an `InsurancePlan` alone; it requires the referenced `InsuranceProduct`, and even then must decide whether to inline the product data or preserve the separate resource with extensions/references.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: During migration, split product-level fields to `InsuranceProduct` and update references/search/indexing that previously targeted `InsurancePlan` product attributes. Review `contact` carefully: the R4 local backbone has similar child concepts, but R6 uses `ExtendedContactDetail` and permits additional organization/period detail.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The move is understandable because these elements describe a product, not a plan-cost variant. However, retaining deprecated fields or providing a formal cross-version extension would have avoided immediate validation failures and made incremental migration easier.

findings.title: Repeatable R4 InsurancePlan.plan backbone was removed and its child plan data was hoisted to the R6 InsurancePlan root

oldState.summary: R4 allowed 0..* plan backbones, each with plan identifier, type, coverageArea, network, generalCost, and specificCost.
oldState.narrativeMd: One R4 `InsurancePlan` resource could contain multiple plan offerings under repeated `plan` elements. Each `plan` carried its own identifiers, classification, service area/network, and cost details.

newState.summary: R6 has no plan backbone. The corresponding plan fields appear at the InsurancePlan root, so each R6 resource represents one plan offering.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 root elements `identifier`, `type`, `coverageArea`, `network`, `generalCost`, and `specificCost` correspond to former R4 `plan.*` content. The repeated plan container itself is gone.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 root plan/cost elements have matching cardinalities and definitions to the former R4 `plan.*` elements, with path changes and minor wording changes.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance containing the `plan` array is invalid as R6. The bigger migration issue is multiplicity: one R4 resource with several `plan` repetitions must become several R6 `InsurancePlan` resources, usually all referencing the same `InsuranceProduct`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrectly collapsing multiple R4 plan repetitions into one R6 resource can mix plan identifiers, group IDs, cost sharing, or network information.

justification.inferredGoal: Make InsurancePlan itself the representation of one plan offering rather than a product container with nested plan offerings.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 `InsurancePlan.plan` backbone as deprecated or allow both nested and root-level plan representations.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Once product information is split out, making each plan offering its own `InsurancePlan` resource is a reasonable model because it improves addressability of plan identifiers, networks, and costs. Keeping the repeatable backbone would avoid old-valid/new-invalid failures, but it would materially compromise that goal by continuing to allow several plan offerings inside one resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking design would retain `InsurancePlan.plan` as deprecated content or permit both nested `plan` data and root plan fields. That alternative covers old R4 instances, including multi-plan resources, but it is partial because it leaves ambiguous representations for the same plan facts and makes it unclear how root fields relate to repeated nested plans.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old multi-plan resources but undermines the one-resource-per-plan model and creates mapping ambiguity.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `InsurancePlan.plan` as 0..* BackboneElement.
R4 plan-level costs live under the repeated plan backbone.
R6 defines general costs directly on InsurancePlan.
R6 uses singular `qualifier` at the hoisted cost path.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 example has two plan repetitions. A faithful R6 migration creates two `InsurancePlan` resources rather than one resource with an array.

findings.narrativeMd: The old repeatable `plan` backbone is gone. This is not just a path rename: R4 allowed a product resource to package multiple plan offerings, while R6 makes each plan offering its own resource. Code that iterates `InsurancePlan.plan[]` must be rewritten around resource-level iteration and product references.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with a `plan` property is R6-invalid. R6 instances can usually be represented in R4 by creating one `plan` repetition under an R4 InsurancePlan, but merging multiple R6 plan resources back to one R4 resource requires grouping by product and may lose resource-level identity and references.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Explode each R4 `plan` repetition into a separate R6 `InsurancePlan`. Move `plan.identifier` to root `identifier`, `plan.type` to root `type`, `plan.coverageArea` to root `coverageArea`, `plan.network` to root `network`, `plan.generalCost` to root `generalCost`, and `plan.specificCost` to root `specificCost`. Rename `qualifiers` to `qualifier` at the cost leaf.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Making plan offerings addressable resources is a strong design rationale, but a transition profile or deprecated `plan` backbone could have supported old data. The downside would be a more complex resource allowing both nested and root plan data.

findings.title: InsurancePlan.type changed from repeatable product type to single plan classification

oldState.summary: R4 root InsurancePlan.type was 0..* and described the kind of health insurance product, with an example binding to insuranceplan-type.

semanticText.definition: The kind of health insurance product.

oldState.narrativeMd: `InsurancePlan.type` in R4 could repeat and represented product category. The actual plan classification was separately available as `InsurancePlan.plan.type`.

newState.summary: R6 InsurancePlan.type is 0..1 and describes plan classification, with no local binding in the InsurancePlan differential.

semanticText.definition: Type of plan. For example, "Platinum" or "High Deductable".

newState.narrativeMd: R6 root `type` corresponds more closely to R4 `plan.type` than to R4 root `type`. Product type is modeled on `InsuranceProduct.type`.

facts.newValue: No binding on R6 InsurancePlan.type; example product type binding moved to InsuranceProduct.type using http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/insuranceproduct-type

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same path exists in both versions, but the R6 short/definition align with the former R4 `InsurancePlan.plan.type`, while R6 `InsuranceProduct.type` carries the product-type value set.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This has a direct validation mechanism: an R4 instance with two or more root `type` values exceeds R6 max 1. Even a single copied value can be semantically wrong because R4 root `type` was product type, not plan classification.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Product/plan type drives product selection, benefit display, and plan-tier classification. Misplacing a product category into a plan tier can mislead downstream logic.

justification.inferredGoal: Make root InsurancePlan.type describe the plan after the plan backbone was hoisted, and move product category to InsuranceProduct.type.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep R4 root `type` as a repeatable product-type alias and add a new plan classification element instead of reusing and narrowing `type`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The product/plan split is reasonable, but this specific path-level break was probably avoidable. R6 could have represented plan classification under a new element while leaving the existing repeatable root `type` available as deprecated product-type content. That would preserve most R4-valid instances and avoid silently treating product categories as plan tiers.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would retain `InsurancePlan.type` at `0..*` for the old product-type meaning, mark it deprecated or transitional, and introduce a distinct plan classification element such as `planType`. The tradeoff is an extra element and a product-type alias that can duplicate `InsuranceProduct.type`, but that is a moderate long-term cost compared with changing the meaning and maximum cardinality of a surviving path.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds legacy surface and duplicates product type with `InsuranceProduct.type`, but avoids a stable path changing meaning and cardinality.

evidence.detail: R4 root type is 0..* CodeableConcept for the kind of product and is summary true.
R4 plan.type is 0..1 CodeableConcept for plan type.
R6 type is 0..1 CodeableConcept and means classification of plan.
R6 product type is represented on InsuranceProduct.type with example insuranceproduct-type binding.

examples.examplesMd: The old root type values should generally migrate to `InsuranceProduct.type`, while R4 `plan.type` values should migrate to R6 `InsurancePlan.type`.

findings.narrativeMd: `InsurancePlan.type` is risky because the path survived but changed role. Validators will catch only the cardinality reduction; they will not catch a semantically wrong transform that copies an R4 product type into the R6 plan classification field.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with multiple root `type` values are old-valid/new-invalid. Instances with one root `type` may validate in R6 but carry the wrong meaning. R6-to-R4 can represent a single plan classification as `plan.type`, but product type must come from `InsuranceProduct.type`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not blindly copy R4 root `type` to R6 `InsurancePlan.type`. Move R4 root `type` to `InsuranceProduct.type`; move R4 `plan.type` to R6 `InsurancePlan.type`; and test both single-type and multi-type product examples.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The narrower R6 field is coherent with one-plan-per-resource, but path reuse makes this likely to break automated mappers. A renamed field or preserved alias would have been easier to migrate.

findings.title: InsurancePlan.identifier kept the path but changed from product identifier to plan/group identifier semantics

oldState.summary: R4 root identifier identified the health insurance product; R4 plan-level identifiers were under InsurancePlan.plan.identifier.

semanticText.definition: Business identifiers assigned to this health insurance product which remain constant as the resource is updated and propagates from server to server.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 had two identifier layers: root product identifiers and nested `plan.identifier` values for individual plan offerings.

newState.summary: R6 InsurancePlan.identifier identifies the plan and/or group; product identifiers belong to InsuranceProduct.identifier.

semanticText.definition: Identifiers, such as the plan ID and/or group ID associated with the insurance plan.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 root identifiers are plan-level identifiers. The R6 definition includes guidance about combinations of plan ID and group ID; product identifiers are stored on `InsuranceProduct.identifier`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 text for `InsurancePlan.identifier` matches the R4 plan-level identifier concept, while R6 `InsuranceProduct.identifier` retains the former product identifier role.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a direct schema validation break because the path, type, and cardinality are still compatible. It is a high runtime and migration risk because automated path-based mappers will preserve syntactically valid but semantically wrong identifiers.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Identifier confusion can merge distinct plans, split one product incorrectly, or break payer/product lookup across systems.

justification.inferredGoal: Use InsurancePlan root identifiers for the now-root plan resource and move product identifiers to InsuranceProduct.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use a new plan identifier path or require explicit identifier typing while preserving old product identifiers separately.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: After R6 narrows `InsurancePlan` to a plan resource, using the root `identifier` to identify that plan is consistent with FHIR resource conventions. A less-breaking design could reduce accidental product-to-plan identifier copying, but only by keeping product identifiers on the plan resource, adding nonstandard element names, or relying on stronger identifier typing rules.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative would add a distinct plan identifier element, such as `planIdentifier`, or require clear identifier type coding while preserving old root product identifiers as transitional content. This is only partial because it either diverges from the expectation that a resource's root `identifier` identifies the resource itself or shifts interoperability burden to profiles and coding discipline.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Reduces semantic mis-migration but conflicts with normal resource identifier conventions or adds profiling burden.

evidence.detail: R4 root identifier definition says it identifies the health insurance product.
R4 plan.identifier definition says it identifies the health insurance plan.
R6 root identifier definition says it is the plan ID and/or group ID associated with the insurance plan.
R6 InsuranceProduct.identifier carries product identifiers.

examples.examplesMd: The example shows why path-based copying is wrong: R4 root identifiers should move to the product; R4 nested plan identifiers should move to the R6 plan root.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a semantic breaking change hidden behind a stable path. A generated model will still accept `InsurancePlan.identifier`, but the identifier no longer identifies the same business object. That is especially dangerous for deduplication and cross-resource matching because validators will not report an error.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with root identifiers remain structurally valid if copied to R6, but the resulting R6 instance may identify the product as though it were a plan. R6-to-R4 conversion must know whether each identifier belongs to the plan or to the product; otherwise it can place plan/group IDs at the old product identifier path.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Build identifier mapping rules based on source path and identifier type/system, not only on element name. Move R4 root `identifier` to `InsuranceProduct.identifier`; move R4 `plan.identifier` to R6 `InsurancePlan.identifier`; and add tests for product ID, plan ID, and group ID combinations.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is mostly unavoidable once `InsurancePlan` becomes the plan resource, but the migration hazard could have been reduced with clearer renaming or normative conversion rules.

findings.title: InsurancePlan-specific invariant requiring identifier or name was removed from InsurancePlan

oldState.summary: R4 InsurancePlan had error invariant ipn-1: identifier.count() + name.count() > 0.

constraints.human: The organization SHALL at least have a name or an idendtifier, and possibly more than one

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 required at least one root identifier or name for the resource. Because `name` was a product-level field, this was effectively a minimum identity rule for the combined product/plan resource.

newState.summary: R6 InsurancePlan has no local ipn-1 invariant; the comparable invariant appears on InsuranceProduct.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `InsurancePlan` can omit `identifier`; it also has no `name` element. The invariant moved with product identity to `InsuranceProduct`, where name and identifier still exist.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R4 InsurancePlan root has local constraint `ipn-1`; the R6 InsurancePlan root does not. R6 InsuranceProduct carries a corrected `ipn-1` invariant with the same expression over product identifier/name.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Removing a constraint is not an R4-to-R6 validation break. It is a round-trip and conformance risk: an R6 `InsurancePlan` with no identifier is valid locally but cannot satisfy the R4 `ipn-1` invariant unless a product name/identifier is merged or a synthetic identifier is introduced.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Identifier-less plans are harder to match, deduplicate, and reconcile across payer systems.

justification.inferredGoal: Move the product identity rule to InsuranceProduct and avoid requiring a plan-level identifier in the base resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because removing the invariant is not an R4-to-R6 old-valid/new-invalid base-design break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R4 invariant depended on `InsurancePlan.name`, which no longer exists on the R6 plan resource, and the comparable product identity rule moved to `InsuranceProduct`. Removing or relocating this constraint does not invalidate R4 instances in R6; the reported concern is mainly that some R6 plans may be hard to down-convert or reconcile without local identifiers.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because this is a constraint weakening and a primarily R6-to-R4 round-trip concern, backward-compatible alternative availability is not applicable. R6 could add a best-practice warning such as `identifier.exists()` for operational quality, but that would intentionally constrain new R6 content rather than preserve old R4-valid instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: A replacement plan-identifier warning could help quality and round-trip conversion, but it would be a new R6 constraint rather than a compatibility alternative.

evidence.detail: R4 InsurancePlan has local error invariant requiring identifier or name.
R6 InsurancePlan differential has no local constraints.
R6 InsuranceProduct carries the identifier-or-name invariant.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment is locally valid with no plan identifier, but a direct R4 InsurancePlan representation would fail the old `ipn-1` rule unless product identity data is merged in.

findings.narrativeMd: The local identity invariant moved off `InsurancePlan`. This is a weakening for R6 validation, but it matters for conversion and operational quality because R6 permits plan resources without a local identifier or name. R4 did not.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No old-valid/new-invalid case is created by removing the invariant. The compatibility problem is R6-valid/not-R4-representable content: an R6 plan with no identifier cannot become a valid R4 InsurancePlan unless the converter also has product name/identifier data or invents an identifier.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When producing R6, preserve plan identifiers whenever available even though the base resource does not require them. When converting back to R4, merge product identity or apply a documented synthetic identifier policy rather than emitting invalid R4 resources.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The old expression could not survive because `name` was removed from `InsurancePlan`. A replacement plan-identifier invariant would have been backward-compatible for high-quality data but might reject legitimate sparse R6 plans.

findings.title: R6 added InsurancePlan.product Reference(InsuranceProduct), creating a new cross-resource dependency not representable in R4

oldState.summary: R4 InsurancePlan had no product reference; product data was inline on the same resource.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented product metadata directly and had no native link from a plan offering to a separate product resource.

newState.summary: R6 InsurancePlan.product is 0..1 Reference(InsuranceProduct) and is summary true.

semanticText.short: The product that this plan is available under
semanticText.definition: The product that this plan is available under.

newState.narrativeMd: The new reference is optional, but it is the intended way to connect a plan to the product that defines benefits and product metadata.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: This is a new R6 element in the InsurancePlan differential with a single target profile: InsuranceProduct.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Adding an optional element does not make R4 data invalid in R6. It does make R6 data harder to express in R4, because R4 has no field for a product reference; preserving meaning requires dereferencing and inlining product data or using an extension.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: A plan without its product may lack the benefit definitions, status, payer ownership, and contacts needed for correct use.

justification.inferredGoal: Connect each plan resource to the reusable product that defines benefits and product metadata.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because `InsurancePlan.product` is an optional additive R6 element and does not make R4 instances invalid.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The optional reference is the natural way to connect the plan resource to the product resource in the normalized R6 model. Its presence creates R6-to-R4 representability and bundling concerns, but it is not itself a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue because old R4 instances are not required to populate it.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Backward-compatible alternative availability is not applicable for this finding. Keeping inline product data or using cross-version extensions may help conversion, but those alternatives relate to the broader product-field removal and down-conversion strategy, not to whether an optional new R6 reference preserves R4-valid instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Down-conversion requires dereferencing, inlining, or extensions, but those are migration mitigations rather than base-design alternatives for this additive element.

evidence.detail: R6 defines product as 0..1 Reference to InsuranceProduct.
evidence.quote: The product that this plan is available under.

evidence.detail: R4 InsurancePlan has no `product` reference element.
The target resource is present in the R6 package as InsuranceProduct.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 reference itself has no R4 equivalent. A converter must either inline the referenced product into an R4 InsurancePlan, preserve it via an extension, or carry both resources with non-core linkage semantics.

findings.narrativeMd: `InsurancePlan.product` is optional but central to the R6 model. Systems that exchange standalone `InsurancePlan` resources must now consider whether the product resource is included or resolvable; otherwise benefit and product metadata may be missing.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is not broken by the optional addition. R6-to-R4 round-tripping is high risk because R4 cannot represent a product link natively, and a strict R4 parser will reject an unknown `product` element.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When generating R6, include `InsuranceProduct` resources in the same transaction/bundle or make their references resolvable. When down-converting, decide whether to dereference and inline product fields, use extensions for the link, or reject incomplete input.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The reference is necessary for the normalized R6 design. Backward compatibility would require keeping the old inline product elements or defining an official cross-version extension for product linkage.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, abstract flag, and `DomainResource` baseDefinition remained stable. The material identity/meaning shift is reported as a finding rather than a literal canonical rename.
No local fixed, pattern, or default value constraints were found on R4 or R6 `InsurancePlan` differential elements.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex value-limit changes were found on compared `InsurancePlan` elements.
No local slicing definitions were present in the R4 or R6 `InsurancePlan` differential elements reviewed.

For surviving/mapped plan-level references, `coverageArea` remains `Reference(Location)` and `network` remains `Reference(Organization)`. The new `product` reference and moved product/admin references are covered in findings.

After accounting for the plan hoist, local cost and plan leaf data types are materially stable (`Identifier`, `CodeableConcept`, `Money`, `Quantity`, `positiveInt`, `string`, and Organization/Location references). The major type/model changes are the removed R4 contact backbone now represented by `ExtendedContactDetail` on `InsuranceProduct`, and the new `product` reference.

The required applicability binding remains on the cost applicability element with the same canonical ValueSet and required strength, but the version changes from `|4.0.1` to `|6.0.0-ballot4` and no live expansion comparison was performed. Product/type binding moves are covered in findings.

No nonstandard serialization-format change was found beyond ordinary FHIR JSON element path changes. The path removals, hoists, singular `qualifier`, and cross-resource split are covered as model/codegen findings.
